description: Single-source lifecycle policy for RedCap-native capabilities, host-exported skills, and portable skill packages.

capability_layers.authority: owns workflow, task ledger, runtime state, validation, closeout, and repo-owned artifacts
thin host entry that imports RedCap core anchors and runs revive/install; it must not fork the rule body
future distribution package generated from the RedCap-native source; host-side copies must remain generated or linked

create: Declare owner, source paths, host exposure, and expected invocation contract before adding a new skill/capability.
version: Record compatibility expectations for RedCap-native source and each host-exported entry before claiming distribution readiness.
install: Prefer symlink or generated host package from this repository; never hand-maintain divergent host copies.
invoke: Document the host-facing trigger, required environment, allowed read/write scope, and fallback behavior.
test: Add a deterministic check or acceptance case for every lifecycle rule that can be machine-enforced.
rollback: Keep a reversible path for generated host entries and portable packages.
deprecate: Mark replacement, sunset reason, and safe migration route before removing active host-facing surfaces.
repair: If a skill is stale, broken, or unsafe, route the finding into Evolution candidates and fix the source-of-truth before updating host mirrors.

rules: Host entries are mirrors and startup anchors, not independent copies of the RedCap rule body.
Active identity anchors must not be exported or mutated by generated host packages.
If a host requires a physical skill directory, prefer symlink or generated copy from this repository and record the adapter boundary.
If a host cannot honor a hook or import instruction, mark that host path degraded rather than duplicating divergent rules.
A skill lifecycle claim is incomplete unless creation, versioning, installation, invocation, testing, rollback, deprecation, and repair have an owner or an explicit degraded boundary.
